explanation: Breadth-first search visits reachable white cells once and records each predecessor. On reaching the destination, follow predecessors back to the start and reverse the path. The input maze is unchanged.
spaceComplexity: O(r · c), including visited cells, predecessors and queue.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Every queued cell is an in-bounds white cell reachable from start through its recorded predecessor chain. Adding a previously unseen orthogonal white neighbor preserves this property and ensures each cell is queued once. Reaching end reconstructs a valid endpoint-inclusive path. If the queue empties, every reachable white cell has been explored, so no path exists.
walkthrough: For maze [[0,0,1],[1,0,0],[0,0,0]], start (0,0) and end (2,2), BFS can discover (0,0)→(0,1)→(1,1)→(2,1)→(2,2). Every step is orthogonal and every visited cell is white, so return that path; the judge validates it as true.
edgeCases: Blocked endpoints cannot be used in a path.
A white start equal to end returns a one-cell path.
Unreachable destinations return an empty list.
The original maze is not modified to mark visits.
